title: Stage coordinator queue overgrowth during canary ramp caused transient mixed-serve and rollback deadlock
creator: Maya Chen
summary: During a staggered canary ramp for runtime-1.22 we observed the stage coordinator's per-stage work queue grow without bound. The backlog caused promotion locks to be held longer than expected, blocking the rollback path and allowing a brief mixed-serve window with stale model shards. The incident lasted ~27 minutes and impacted throughput and returned inconsistent model versions for a subset of requests.
impact: User-facing latency spikes and inconsistent model outputs for approximately 10% of requests routed through the affected region for 27 minutes. No customer data was leaked; primary impact is reliability and incorrect responses for low-latency production features.
detection: Automated alert on stage-coordinator-queue-length (> 10k) fired at 2026-03-10T14:11:12Z. SRE on-call correlated increased 99th latency and surge in promotion lock hold times from traces. First human ack at 14:13 UTC.
timeline:
2026-03-10 14:07 UTC: Canary ramp started (stage coordinator received burst of promotion jobs)
2026-03-10 14:11 UTC: Queue length alert (stage-coordinator-queue-length > 10k)
2026-03-10 14:12 UTC: 99th percentile latency increases observed; traces show promotion lock hold times rising
2026-03-10 14:13 UTC: SRE starts manual mitigation; attempt to trigger rollback via control-plane API returned 500 due to promotion lock deadlock
2026-03-10 14:18 UTC: Team triages; manually drain coordinator queue using emergency drain job; partial relief
2026-03-10 14:24 UTC: KV cache invalidation jobs lagging behind; stale shards served briefly while promotion and shard resync raced
2026-03-10 14:34 UTC: Coordinator queue drained; rollback completed successfully and stable state restored
2026-03-10 14:40 UTC: Post-incident monitoring show normal metrics
root_cause: A combination of factors: (1) The stage coordinator lacked backpressure to ingress and would enqueue promotion/resync jobs without upper-bound throttles. (2) Promotion lock acquisition code held locks across an I/O path that occasionally stalled (resync of shard manifests), amplifying hold time when the queue was large. (3) KV cache invalidation is performed asynchronously but depends on order guarantees that were violated when the promotion path was delayed, enabling transient serve of stale shards. (4) The rollback path attempted to acquire the same locks and if locks were held by stuck resync jobs, rollback failed (deadlock-like behavior).
mitigations: Emergency: manual drain job to dequeue non-critical promotion tasks and prioritize rollback tasks
Short-term: increased alert sensitivity on promotion-lock-hold-time and queue-growing-derivative to detect runaway early
Short-term: adjust autoscaler to add headroom for coordinator workers in that region during canary ramps
action_items: Omar Delgado: Implement per-stage queue soft-cap and backpressure to ingress (limit enqueues and return 429 when coordinator overloaded). Due: 2026-03-21
Maya Chen: Refactor promotion lock to avoid holding across network I/O; acquire-retry pattern and lease with bounded hold time. Due: 2026-04-04
Priya Nair: Make rollback path preemptive for promotion/resync jobs (priority inversion fix) and add unit/integration tests for lock interleavings. Due: 2026-03-28
SRE Team (on-call rotation): Add alert and runbook entry for stage-coordinator-queue-length and promotion-lock-hold-time with explicit remediation steps. Due: 2026-03-17
Platform QA: Add e2e chaos test that simulates slow shard resync during high canary ramp to verify preemptive rollback succeeds. Due: 2026-04-11
notes: This incident exposed a systemic gap in how we prioritize control-plane operations under load. The safe-unwind plan (preemptive rollback) needs to be codified as platform invariants rather than ad-hoc scripts. Consider surfacing coordinator health to the Console's rollout page.
followups: Design: Update Console UX to show per-stage queue length and 'rollback-preemptive-capable' flag
Product: Add rollout guidance for customers recommending staged ramps with coordinator headroom settings
Infra: Evaluate region capacity reservation during scheduled canary ramps to avoid autoscaler delays
